overall: Council violated the Law by deliberating outside a posted meeting on a joint resignation-call statement and by approving minutes that did not summarize public comment; notices and other claims were not violations.

allegations.summary: A quorum of Councilors allegedly coordinated outside a posted meeting on a joint statement calling for a colleague's resignation, issued on or around November 20.
Alleged deliberations outside posted meetings to pressure federal officials, fill a seat, table agenda items, and censure a councilor.
allegations.key_passage: After review, we find insufficient evidence of such deliberation.

allegations.summary: Notices for the November 21, December 5, and December 12 meetings allegedly lacked enough detail about the preceding meetings' minutes to be approved.
allegations.key_passage: Where each of the three meeting notices at issue in the complaints identified the specific meeting minutes to be reviewed and approved, we find that the notices were sufficiently specific in this regard and the Council did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Minutes of the November 14, November 21, and December 5 meetings allegedly listed registered public speakers without summarizing their comments.
allegations.key_passage: Here, the meeting minutes contain nothing more than a list of names of registered speakers who spoke on various topics, without any summary of their comments.

allegations.summary: Generalized claims that the minutes were insufficient in other respects, including omitted dissenting views, without identifying particular deficiencies.
allegations.key_passage: we decline to review such allegations.

allegations.summary: Allegations that documents were leaked, voters were disenfranchised, and the Council gave up its authority, which would not violate the Law even if true.
allegations.key_passage: we decline to review allegations that, even if true, would not constitute violations of the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
Within 45 days of the letter, amend the minutes of the November 14, November 21, and December 5 meetings to summarize public comment received during the meetings
remedy_passage: We order the Council’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution the Council that a determination by our office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
